description: Live proof of the AI Workshop re-solve fix. Same "clean it up" request that previously published a fudged 166deg now returns the solver-verified 178deg.
question: From external point $P$, a tangent touches circle $O$ at point $T$, and a secant passes through the circle intersecting it at points $A$ and $B$ (with $A$ between $P$ and $B$). The far arc $\overset{\frown}{TB}$ (not containing $A$) measures $(8x + 6)°$, and the near arc $\overset{\frown}{TA}$ (between the tangent and secant on the near side) measures $(4x - 2)°$. The angle formed at $P$ is $\angle TPB = 47°$. Using the secant–tangent angle theorem, set up and solve an equation to find the degree measure of arc $\overset{\frown}{TB}$.

solution_steps.title: Understand the Setup
solution_steps.description:
From external point $P$, a **tangent** touches the circle at $T$ and a **secant** cuts through at $A$ (near) then $B$ (far).

The key relationship here is the **Secant–Tangent Angle Theorem**:
$$\angle P = \frac{1}{2}\bigl(\text{far arc} - \text{near arc}\bigr)$$
The angle at the outside point always equals **half the difference** of the two arcs it intercepts — the bigger arc it "sees" minus the smaller one.

Here:
- Far arc: $\overset{\frown}{TB} = (8x + 6)°$
- Near arc: $\overset{\frown}{TA} = (4x - 2)°$
- Angle at $P$: $47°$

solution_steps.title: Set Up the Equation
solution_steps.description:
Plug everything into the theorem:
$$47 = \frac{1}{2}\bigl[(8x + 6) - (4x - 2)\bigr]$$
Subtracting distributes the minus sign across $(4x - 2)$:
$$47 = \frac{1}{2}\bigl[8x + 6 - 4x + 2\bigr] = \frac{1}{2}(4x + 8)$$

solution_steps.title: Solve for x
solution_steps.description:
Multiply both sides by $2$ to clear the fraction:
$$94 = 4x + 8$$
Subtract $8$:
$$86 = 4x$$
Divide by $4$:
$$x = 21.5$$

solution_steps.title: Find Arc TB
solution_steps.description:
Substitute $x = 21.5$ into the far arc expression:
$$\overset{\frown}{TB} = 8(21.5) + 6 = 172 + 6 = 178°$$

A quick sanity check — near arc $\overset{\frown}{TA} = 4(21.5) - 2 = 86 - 2 = 84°$, and indeed $\tfrac{1}{2}(178 - 84) = \tfrac{1}{2}(94) = 47°$ ✓
